content:
Jamal: heads-up, eu-west streaming p99 jumped from 240ms -> 1.8s around 17:02 UTC, streaming queue depth at 120 and climbing. non-streaming sync jobs occupying many GPU slots. infra-bot: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streams eu-west queue_depth 120, gpu_util 92%
Sara: saw this too, root cause seems to be long non-streaming batches (>2k tokens) holding KV caches and preventing slot turnover. current allocator is single FIFO across streaming+sync.
Kevin: yeah this matches the replay from yesterday where sync jobs starved streaming. we need a fairness/admission change, not just more capacity.
Anya: product note — streaming p99 is a visible SLA for a few customers, need a fix that doesn't drop synchronous throughput for queued enterprise jobs without warning.
Jamal: short-term idea: reserve N streaming slots per shard in eu-west (e.g., 15% of slots) and add a small per-mode rate limiter. cheaper than lifting global capacity. thoughts?
Sara: agree. propose config patch for admission-controller:
```
{
  "admission": {
    "mode_priorities": ["streaming","sync"],
    "reservations": {"streaming": "0.15"},
    "preempt": {"enabled": true, "min_age_s": 60, "target_free": 1}
  }
}
```
Kevin: preemption helps but careful: killing sync jobs loses work and may cause retries which are expensive. Recommend preempt only if job age > 60s and we first try soft-eviction (pause/backoff).
Jamal: good call. add metrics so we know how often preempt happens. add tag preempted=true and reason=slot-reserve.
Anya: from product side, if we preempt enterprise customer jobs we need to surface a graceful error and a follow-up retry/backoff doc. also potential billing implications.
Kevin: billing note — preemption might double-charge if we don't prorate. ops/finance should decide proration policy.
Sara: implementation plan: 1) config change to reserve streaming slices in eu-west only, 2) add metrics and preemption telemetry, 3) soft-evict flow (pause / ask client to retry with Retry-After), 4) gradual rollout to 10% of shards -> monitor.
Jamal: can we route non-critical sync workloads to other regions (us-west) as spillover? we have capacity there at 60% util.
Sara: yes, smart-routing can be used but needs policy: only on non-data-resident models. we can add region preference tag to admission config.
infra-bot: queued rollout job created: rollout/adm-change-euw-reserve, target_shards=12, step=canary(1), metrics=[streaming_p99,stream_qd,preempt_count].
deploy-bot: started canary deploy of adm-controller v3.7.1 to shard euw-12.
Jamal: I'll watch streaming_p99 and stream_qd, will post updates. if streaming_p99 < 400ms after canary we ramp.
Kevin: capture cost delta in the first hour. reserving slots reduces overall throughput efficiency; we need numbers to justify sustained policy.
Anya: ok. I'll draft a short customer comms template in case any enterprise hits soft-evict.
Jamal: thanks. if canary looks good we'll roll to all eu-west shards in 30m.
Sara: noted — adding log lines for preempt reason and client hint header 'X-Redwood-Backpressure: streaming-reserve'
Jamal: update 17:08 UTC canary looks promising, stream_qd down to 18, p99 ~360ms. will continue monitoring.
Jamal: update 17:17 UTC preempt_count=3 on canary shard, all soft-evicts, no client retries yet. continuing.
Jamal: update 17:30 UTC rolling to 50% shards.
Jamal: 17:40 UTC rolling complete for eu-west. streaming p99 stabilized around 330-420ms. leaving reservations enabled.
Anya: thank you team. follow-ups: billing decision and docs for soft-evict behavior.
Kevin: opened PERF ticket to model cost vs reserved fraction and find optimal threshold. ticket: https://github.com/redwood/perf/issues/402
Jamal: closing thread, will open postmortem if we see regressions.
